attendees.role: director, Lunenburg Adult Activity Center / COA

budget_items.what_was_said: The Eagle House supporters announced their annual Festival of Trees fundraiser benefiting LAAC programs and services, with tree/basket donation deadlines and bidding dates in November. The board discussed whether to contribute a decorated tree again as it did last year.

budget_items.topic: Friendly neighbors (Shogun neighbors) network program cost
budget_items.what_was_said: The director reported researching a multi-town friendly-neighbors program with a membership cost, but found it duplicated services already offered here and had a long waiting list.
The board discussed confusion over the current gift fund balance versus a figure given previously by the town, with the treasurer saying she was still awaiting clarification from town hall.
A board member noted the gift fund had received relatively modest donations this past year aside from the women's club and premise seniors contributions.
A donation attributed to Adams's daughter was clarified as going to the House (Eagle House), not to the Council on Aging directly.

A board member explained that a capital planning request must be for a tangible asset with multi-year use and above a stated dollar threshold, in the context of pursuing funding for the parking lot design.

budget_items.topic: Eagle House toll booth fundraiser goal
budget_items.what_was_said: Eagle House Supporters described an upcoming toll booth fundraiser on October 24th with a stated fundraising goal.

budget_items.topic: Eagle House Supporters fundraising goal increase for FY27
budget_items.what_was_said: At their annual meeting, Eagle House Supporters voted to raise their fundraising goal for FY27 and beyond to help offset the town budget going to the center.

budget_items.topic: Eagle House Supporters overall annual fundraising goal
budget_items.what_was_said: Nicole Waters stated the group's overall annual fundraising goal, which includes the annual mailing appeal in addition to events.

budget_items.topic: Town funding to Eagle House Supporters-supported programs
budget_items.what_was_said: A board member noted that town funding for the programs Eagle House Supporters helps fund was reduced this year compared to last year, underscoring the value of the group's fundraising.

decisions.decision: Invited new outreach coordinator Jan Robbins to sit at the table and introduce herself to the public.
Decided not to pursue joining the multi-town friendly-neighbors network and instead to revitalize and expand the center's existing friendly visitors program.
Director authorized to order engraved plaques with the Council's own logo for Century Club and Boston Post Cane honorees.
Chair will follow up with the (newly reconvened) bylaw committee about formalizing honorary-member status, including that honorary members do not vote.
Director agreed to send the FY26 year-end financial report to the board before the next meeting, and to try to produce quarterly reports going forward.
Agreed to add review of the policies and procedures packet as an agenda item for the next meeting.
Agreed to hold off reposting the policies and procedures packet online until it has been reviewed, updated, and re-voted on.
Agreed to pursue a capital planning request for the senior center parking lot design/construction funding.
Chair will ask the town's regional ambassador contact (Margaret) whether Lunenburg can be included in the new Groten UMass facility's ambulance catchment area.
Board members asked to check their entries on the contact list and report corrections to Michelle so it can be resent.

minutes.summary: This Council on Aging meeting covered mostly routine business: introducing new outreach coordinator Jan Robbins, discussing whether the board should submit its own annual town report entry separate from the director's operational report, reviewing honorary-member bylaw questions, and hearing updates on SHINE counseling coverage, a parking lot/ADA accessibility project, the 41A senior tax exemption outreach campaign, and a new UMass emergency facility in Groton. The board also heard financial and fundraising reports, including confusion over the gift fund balance, and closed with a tribute to Dolly Parton's caregiving advocacy and a group photo.
